claim: Onasemnogene abeparvovec gene therapy improves survival and motor function in infants with spinal muscular atrophy type 1
gold_rationale: Clinical and regulatory consensus is unambiguously SUPPORTED. SMA type 1 has a uniformly fatal natural history: untreated, ~8% are event-free at 20 months (START historical cohort) and only ~25% survive free of permanent ventilation beyond 14 months (FDA-cited natural history); independent sitting is essentially never achieved (0/23 in the PNCR control). Across START phase 1 (N=15) and the pivotal single-arm phase 3 STR1VE-US (N=22) and STR1VE-EU (N=32 ITT), 91-97% of treated infants survived free of permanent ventilation at 14 months (vs 26% PNCR, p<0.0001) and a substantial fraction achieved independent sitting (59% US, 44% EU) never seen untreated. SPR1NT confirmed the effect in presymptomatic infants. This is a genuine all-or-none / very-large effect in a lethal disease where single-arm evidence against a well-characterized fatal natural history is the accepted evidentiary standard - the basis on which the FDA granted REGULAR (not accelerated) approval of Zolgensma (BLA 125694) on 24 May 2019 on the co-primary endpoints of survival and sitting without support. No randomized trial contradicts the claim; the surrogate concern does not apply because survival free of permanent ventilation is a hard clinical endpoint. Verdict = Supported (dramatic-effect / all-or-none exemption applies).
outcome: Survival free of permanent ventilation and achievement of motor milestones (independent sitting; CHOP INTEND motor function)
population: Symptomatic infantile-onset spinal muscular atrophy type 1 infants (biallelic SMN1 mutation, typically 2 copies SMN2, onset before 6 months)

rows.citation: Day JW, Finkel RS, Chiriboga CA, et al. Onasemnogene abeparvovec gene therapy for symptomatic infantile-onset spinal muscular atrophy in patients with two copies of SMN2 (STR1VE): an open-label, single-arm, multicentre, phase 3 trial. Lancet Neurol. 2021;20(4):284-293. DOI:10.1016/S1474-4422(21)00001-6 (NCT03306277).
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed PMID 33743238: pivotal phase 3 single-arm US trial vs PNCR natural-history cohort. Design coded 'rct' as nearest interventional enum; actually single-arm open-label.
rows.finding: 20/22 (91%) survived free from permanent ventilation at 14 months vs 6/23 (26%) untreated PNCR cohort (p<0.0001); 13/22 (59%) achieved independent sitting >=30s vs 0/23 (p<0.0001).

rows.citation: Mercuri E, Muntoni F, Baranello G, et al. Onasemnogene abeparvovec gene therapy for symptomatic infantile-onset spinal muscular atrophy type 1 (STR1VE-EU): an open-label, single-arm, multicentre, phase 3 trial. Lancet Neurol. 2021;20(10):832-841. DOI:10.1016/S1474-4422(21)00251-9 (NCT03461289).
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed PMID 34536405: European pivotal phase 3 single-arm trial, broader eligibility than STR1VE-US; vs PNCR control. 33 dosed, 32 ITT (one excluded for dosing at day 181). Coded 'rct'; actually single-arm open-label.
rows.finding: 31/32 (97%) survived free from permanent ventilation at 14 months vs 6/23 (26%) PNCR cohort (p<0.0001); 14/32 (44%) achieved independent sitting >=10s vs 0/23 (p<0.0001). One death was unrelated to study drug.

rows.citation: Mendell JR, Al-Zaidy S, Shell R, et al. Single-Dose Gene-Replacement Therapy for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (START phase 1/2). N Engl J Med. 2017;377(18):1713-1722. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1706198 (NCT02122952).
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed PMID 29091557: first-in-human phase 1/2 ascending-dose single-arm study; historical-control comparison (~8% survival). Coded 'rct' as nearest interventional enum; actually single-arm phase 1/2.
rows.finding: All 15 patients alive and event-free at 20 months of age vs 8% survival in historical cohort; high-dose cohort CHOP INTEND rose +15.4 points at 3 months; 11/12 sat unassisted and 2 walked independently - outcomes never seen in untreated SMA1.

rows.citation: STR1VE (AVXS-101-CL-303): Study of Intravenous Onasemnogene Abeparvovec-xioi in Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type 1. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03306277 (completed). Primary study underlying FDA approval and Day 2021 Lancet Neurol.
rows.integrity_note: Verified via ClinicalTrials.gov: phase 3, open-label, single-arm, single-dose, completed 2019-11-12, N=22, co-primary endpoints independent sitting >=30s and event-free survival. Coded 'rct' as nearest interventional enum.
rows.finding: Registered pivotal single-arm trial (completed) whose survival and sitting endpoints formed the primary basis of FDA regular approval; corroborates the published STR1VE-US results.

rows.citation: Strauss KA, Farrar MA, Muntoni F, et al. Onasemnogene abeparvovec for presymptomatic infants with three copies of SMN2 at risk for spinal muscular atrophy: the Phase III SPR1NT trial. Nat Med. 2022;28(7):1390-1397. DOI:10.1038/s41591-022-01867-3 (NCT03505099).
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed PMID 35715567: presymptomatic (not symptomatic SMA1) cohort, 3 SMN2 copies - population_match=false; included as convergent supportive evidence. Coded 'rct'; single-arm.
rows.finding: All 15 presymptomatic children (3 SMN2 copies) survived without permanent ventilation at 14 months; all stood independently and 14/15 walked independently (p<0.0001), most within normal developmental windows - supports directionality but off-population.

rows.citation: Toro W, Reyna SP, Ritter S, et al. Early Intervention and Speed-to-Effect in SMA Type 1 Following Onasemnogene Abeparvovec: Pooled Post-Hoc Analysis (START, STR1VE-US, STR1VE-EU). Neurol Ther. 2025;14(5):1903-1918. DOI:10.1007/s40120-025-00791-1.
rows.integrity_note: Verified via PubMed PMID 40622452: Novartis-sponsored pooled post-hoc analysis of the three symptomatic SMA1 trials; industry-funded, weighted as supportive synthesis. dramatic_effect=false to avoid double-counting the pivotal trials.
rows.finding: Pooled N=67 symptomatic SMA1 non-sitters: 54/59 (91.5%) achieved clinically significant >=4-point CHOP INTEND gain by 6 months; ventilation-free survival significantly exceeded natural history throughout follow-up.

Regular (not accelerated) approval on co-primary survival + sitting-without-support endpoints; efficacy vs natural history (~25% survival, sitting never expected untreated). Real checkable identifier BLA 125694; prior fabricated-DOI source_id corrected.
rows.finding: FDA granted regular approval for children <2 years with SMA (biallelic SMN1 mutations) based on improvement in survival and achievement of motor milestones (sitting without support >=30s) in the phase 3 trial supported by phase 1; boxed warning for serious liver injury is the principal managed risk.

baseline.text: Yes. Onasemnogene abeparvovec (Zolgensma) clearly improves survival and motor function in infants with SMA type 1. Untreated SMA1 is nearly uniformly fatal - roughly 90%+ of infants die or need permanent ventilation by age 2, with only ~8% event-free survival at 20 months. In the START phase 1 study all 15 treated infants were alive and event-free at 20 months, and in the pivotal single-arm phase 3 trials STR1VE-US and STR1VE-EU roughly 91-97% survived free of permanent ventilation at 14 months and a substantial fraction achieved independent sitting - a milestone never observed in untreated SMA1. On this basis the FDA granted regular approval in 2019. This is a classic all-or-none effect against a fatal natural history, so single-arm evidence is considered definitive. The main safety concern is acute liver injury/transaminase elevation, managed with corticosteroids.
